newsitem.title: USA: Salomon February same store sales index up 4.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Salomon February same store sales index up 4.7 pct.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said its same store sales growth index rose 4.7 percent in February, compared with 7.3 percent in January and a 5.2 percent gain a year ago.
February sales were positively affected by a continuation of solid underlying macroeconomic fundamentals and more seasonal weather, which aided apparel sales, Salomon Brothers said in a report.
February retail sales maintained the momentum generated in January, the report said.
Salomon Brothers said it expects retailers to continue to benefit from steady economic expansion, relatively low levels of interest rates and continued moderate inflation in 1997.

Salomon Brothers also said it expects retailers to benefit from strong inventory and expense controls which will lead these companies' earnings to outpace the earnings of the S&P 500 companies beginning in the second or, at the latest, third quarter of 1997.
